topic: differential privacy; graph algorithms; synthetic graph release
status: historical open-problem progression; guarantee comparison required
claim: The 2011/2012 Iterative Constructions and Private Data Release paper gives a pure-DP synthetic-graph cut-query error bound of O(n^1.5/epsilon) and identifies a private rank-1-approximation route as an open path to improvement. The 2025 Breaking the n^1.5 Barrier paper uses private expander decomposition to achieve a polynomial-time sparse synthetic graph with n^(1.25+o(1)) additive error together with (1+gamma) multiplicative error under approximate (epsilon,delta)-DP. This advances a related sparse-cut-sparsifier frontier, but is not an apples-to-apples improvement under the same privacy and error guarantee.

sources.title: Iterative Constructions and Private Data Release
locators: §§1 and 5: IDC framework and Frieze/Kannan interactive cut-query bound
§§6–7: pure-DP synthetic graph with O(n^1.5/epsilon) additive error and rank-1 approximation open route

sources.title: Breaking the n^1.5 Additive Error Barrier for Private and Efficient Graph Sparsification via Private Expander Decomposition
locators: §1, Table 1, Theorem 1.1: prior n^1.5 frontier and approximate-DP sparse synthetic graph n^(1.25+o(1)) additive plus multiplicative error
§6: remaining n^1.25 and graph-density open questions

interpretation: This is a documented multi-year theoretical progression and a useful example of how an explicitly named frontier can move. The 2025 result changes the guarantee (approximate DP and multiplicative-plus-additive error) and sparsity conditions; it does not simply improve the 2011 pure-DP additive bound under identical assumptions. No empirical utility experiment or independent proof verification was performed here.
falsifiable_question: For fixed graph families, edge-neighboring model, epsilon/delta, sparsity, and multiplicative tolerance, in which density regimes does private expander decomposition strictly improve worst-case cut error over earlier mechanisms? Does any improvement remain under pure DP or purely additive error?
primary_outcome: Theorem-level worst-case all-cut additive error, multiplicative distortion, privacy parameters, sparsity, and runtime compared under explicitly matched assumptions.
counterevidence_and_caveats: The 2011 paper appeared at TCC 2012; arXiv upload is not its venue-publication year.
Pure DP versus approximate DP is a material difference.
The 2025 result includes multiplicative error and a sparse-output requirement; its n^1.25 exponent is not directly comparable to a pure additive n^1.5 bound without aligning assumptions.
Both works are theoretical; this audit is not a proof verification or empirical graph-utility replication.
suggested_design: Construct a theorem-comparison table for graph density, weight assumptions, edge adjacency, pure/approximate DP, multiplicative tolerance, output sparsity, failure probability, and constants/polylog factors. Then target only parameter regimes with non-overlapping guarantees; separately implement and benchmark algorithms on generated and public graph families without presenting experiments as theorem verification.
